headline: Warming has already slowed agricultural productivity growth and generally reduces major-crop yields, but outcomes depend on crop, location, CO2 fertilization, water, adaptation, pests, markets, and socioeconomic conditions.

historical_attribution.study_interpretation: A modeled slowing of cumulative productivity growth relative to a no-anthropogenic-climate-change counterfactual; not 21 percent less current food production.

not_supported: Describing the 21 percent productivity-growth slowdown as a 21 percent loss of food.
Applying the Zhao et al. per-degree values while silently assuming CO2 fertilization or adaptation.
Equating crop yield with food security; access, prices, distribution, nutrition, and conflict also matter.
